quote: The MinION has a clear PMMA (i.e., acrylic) case, which will not be acceptable for Exploration environments due to flammability concerns.

The foam insulation is a silicone, but the specific foam is not identified. The exposed foam has a fire-retardant coating for ISS 24.1% O2, suggesting that it will be flammable in all Exploration atmospheres.
Armaflex AP is used as pipe insulation on CDRA and passes flammability in 30% O2. However, when covered by the black KB 10 tape, the configuration is flammable (F-12d) [ref. 92].

Exposed materials appear to be metallic with the exception of Teflon-insulated electrical wiring, the Dapco 2030-coated compressor fiberglass-epoxy composite acoustic cover, and a silicone duct. The acoustic cover and duct are nonflammable in 30% O2, 10.2 psia, but likely to be flammable in 34-40% O2 at 8.2 psia.

hardware: Emergency Mask, Fire, and Ammonia Cartridges
quote: Orange Nomex bags are used to store the emergency masks, ammonia cartridges, and fire cartridges. This material is nonflammable for up to 30% O2 10.2 psia, but would have to be modified for 34-40% O2 at 8.2 psia (e.g., fire retardant treatment) (F-12f).
Silicones are usually flammable in 30% O2, 10.2 psia, but Bisco HT-200A is nonflammable to at least 34% O2.
The Velcro strips inside the fecal canister are longer than allowed by the standard Velcro rules [ref. 21], but are internal to the canister and not considered a concern.
Electrical cables are Teflon-insulated and nonflammable beyond 40% O2.
The polycarbonate display window will be acceptable for flammability in Exploration atmospheres to 30% O2 at 10.2 psia, but will be flammable at higher O2 concentrations.
The CAD body is made of Ultem 1000, which is not flammable in 30% O2 at 10.2 psia, but flammable in 34-40% O2 at 8.2 psia.
The CWQMK is contained in a pouch, the outer surface of which is Durette fabric, acceptable for flammability at O2 concentrations up to 30% at 10.2 psia, but not for higher concentrations.

The device strap used by the crew is nylon, which is flammable, but acceptable for MPCV 30% O2 at 10.2 psia because it is crew-tended when in use and, when not in use, contained in the flywheel housing and exposed to the environment for only about 2 in. at the handle connection point.
The CQ side walls and kick panels are constructed of 1-in.-thick sandwich composite panels with a Nomex honeycomb core. This design is acceptable for flammability in 30% O2, 10.2 psia [ref. 103].

The internal heater assembly contains Kapton heaters, an Aerogel blanket, and melamine foam insulation, but would be acceptable for flammability in Exploration atmospheres because the flammable materials are enclosed by nonflammable Aerogel blanket and anodized aluminum housing.
Inside the suitcase, the Mosites 10298-coated melamine foam is a concern for flammability in 34-40% O2, 8.2 psia, but not in 30% O2, 10.2 psia.
NASA has limited material flammability data at O2 concentration higher than 30% (F-12a).

Specifically, nominal cabin atmospheres of 10.2 pounds per square inch absolute (psia) with 26.5% O2, and 8.2 psia with 34% O2, collectively termed “Exploration Atmospheres” here to differentiate from ISS nominal atmosphere, were considered.

A total of 33 subsystems and/or components within the ECLSS, including emergency systems, Crew Health Care Systems (CHeCS), and Crew Habitation Systems, were evaluated using available design data and historical literature.
